original_card.question: Can one measured replay bottleneck be sped up without dropping coverage?
methods: Profile one isolated replay and optimize the measured bottleneck.
Design source-bound reuse with explicit dependency invalidation and negative controls.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Report before/after wall time on the same fixture, retained checks and invalidation behavior.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Measure one unchanged fixture, preserve check coverage, and test one optimization with invalidation controls.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Faster trustworthy replays increase review throughput and let mechanism candidates be checked sooner.
allowed_variations: Profile one stage or design one source-bound cache boundary.
scope_change_triggers: Skipping coverage or comparing different fixtures to claim speedup.

actual_scope: On the 36 E6 lines stored as the A2 complement in the shadow witness, does low_weight_words return exactly the weight-at-most-16 words of the 7-dimensional F2 incidence code of the 135 orthogonal 4-frames?
scope_change_reason: The replay-runtime card asks for a new measured speedup. The revision-8 verification row says a published faster replay is not equivalent coverage until checked. The merged E7 kernel comparison already did that for one code, and the orbit partition of that same support set is already delivered. This package checks the remaining unbound code named by that handoff: the E6 4-frame incidence code. It does not time an engine or install one.
bottleneck_link: Deletion and decoder certificates reuse this iterator only if a second code still returns every low-weight word. This comparison binds that iterator to the E6 frame code. It does not change a supplier bill or kappa.
stop_rule: Stop after one set comparison of the published engine against a literal doubling and two half-splits of this kernel. Do not remeasure timings, rerun the 27-dimensional E7 census, or search another root system.
evidence: The incidence matrix of 135 orthogonal 4-frames on the 36 stored E6 lines has F2 rank 29 and kernel dimension 7, with free coordinates (0, 1, 2, 4, 6, 8, 20). A literal doubling and half-splits at dimensions 3 and 4 agree on 64 words of weight at most 16: zero plus 63 weight-16 words, and no lighter nonzero word, over all 128 codewords. low_weight_words at batch sizes 16 and 8 returns that set. Weight bound 15 returns only zero. A dropped support, an injected weight-15 word, and a repeated generator fail.
author: unpaidmoon

open_questions.question: Does the same set equality hold for one D6 or P112 punctured frame code, at a named width and weight bound?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The E6 check does not transfer to a different deletion. The bit-lane proof still leaves every other consumer unbound.
open_questions.first_step: Build that incidence kernel from a pinned root list, then compare one half-split with low_weight_words on that basis alone.
open_questions.blocked_by: No second root list is pinned in this package.

open_questions.question: Does the opt-in intersection-counter engine return this same 64-word set?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A faster substitute is not coverage for this code until the sets are compared. Production replacement remains a separate installation.
open_questions.first_step: Run research/e7-intersection-counters/engine.py on this 7-generator basis at one batch size and compare it with the set hashed here.
open_questions.blocked_by: This package does not load that engine.
